mechanism_narrative: The current level of CPIAUCSL (inflation index) is negatively correlated with S&P 500 20-day forward returns. Higher inflation levels compress real equity valuations and increase monetary policy tightening expectations, leading to negative returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL > 195 (t-test p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The current level of FEDFUNDS (federal funds rate) is negatively correlated with S&P 500 20-day forward returns. Higher interest rates reduce the present value of future equity cash flows and increase the cost of capital, leading to negative returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS > 3.5% (t-test p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 5.0%, it signals a tight labor market and strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns. This condition is active only when unemployment is below the threshold.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when UNRATE < 5.0% (t-test p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 2000 units, it signals strong consumer demand and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns. This condition is active only when housing starts are above the threshold.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST > 2000 (t-test p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL drives S&P 500 returns. When FEDFUNDS is rising and CPIAUCSL is above 195, it signals a monetary tightening cycle that compresses equity valuations, leading to negative returns. The signal is active only when both conditions are met.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS rising and CPIAUCSL > 195 (t-test p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between industrial production (INDPRO) and employment (PAYEMS) drives S&P 500 returns. When INDPRO is rising and PAYEMS is above 134000, it signals a strong economy with rising inflation, leading to negative returns as the Fed may tighten policy. The signal is active only when both conditions are met.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO rising and PAYEMS > 134000 (t-test p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes (defined by GDP growth > 2% and unemployment rate < 5.0%), a rise in housing starts (HOUST) above 2000 units signals strong consumer demand and positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns. The signal is active only within this regime.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST > 2000 and regime condition met (t-test p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles (defined by CPIAUCSL > 195), the current level of CPIAUCSL is negatively correlated with S&P 500 5-day forward returns. High inflation levels trigger aggressive monetary policy, leading to negative returns in the short term.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL > 195 (t-test p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.
